old_oromir_10.m: [Thoughtful, but resolute.] Different? Yes, I suppose we are. A weight I didn't even know I carried has been lifted. I feel stronger now, more alive than ever before.

old_oromir_20.m: [Firmly, but not unkindly.] What happened doesn't matter anymore. What matters is that the darkness is gone, and we can finally live. You should do the same. Let it rest. Ease your mind and later, if you still have questions, please visit us then.

old_oromir_and_leta_narrator_10.m:
While looking between Leta and Oromir, you are unsettled by their calm acceptance. The house feels peaceful, but the air is heavy with unanswered questions.

Leta and Oromir's transformations are undeniable. Their peace is haunting, a reminder that not all wounds leave visible scars. The spirit may be gone, but its mark remains.

old_oromir_initial_phrase.m: [Calm, almost welcoming.] Ah, there you are. You've come back to see us, then.
r: Oromir? What happened to you two? You look...different.
Oh, it's still so hard to see you like this. But I still have questions.

old_oromir_leta_responds_10.m: [frail, but smiling warmly] Don't mind him, dear. He's always been dramatic. I may not remember everything, but I know this much--I finally feel at peace.
r: Leta...this isn't normal. You look like you've aged decades overnight. How can you be so calm about this?

old_oromir_leta_responds_20.m: Oh, time catches up to us all, doesn't it? Better to find peace than cling to what's already gone. Whatever you did, thank you. Truly.
r: I didn't do this to you. This doesn't feel right. What happened after the spirit was defeated?

old_oromir_questions_10.m: [With a gentle smile.] Of course. Ask what you will. We owe you that much.
r: Why were you affected too? Leta was the one possessed by the spirit, not you.
In your basement, I talked to a man, a farmer-looking man that is. I suspect that he is your child. But he is frightened and confused...

old_oromir_questions_bond_10.m: Well, my child, you see, once I entered into the sacred bond of marriage with Leta, I too became bound to the spirit. Our lives, our fates, were entwined by the very vows we spoke. When she was touched by its darkness, I could not help but share in the burden.
r: So, the bond between you two extended even to the curse?

old_oromir_questions_bond_10n.m: While sighing, his voice remains steady.

old_oromir_questions_bond_20.m: Yes. That's the nature of true union, is it not? In love and in struggle, we are as one. Her pain became mine, just as her redemption became ours. The spirit's malice sought to age us, to wear us down. But we endure, thanks to you.
r: Do you regret it? Being tied to her curse?

old_oromir_questions_bond_30.m: Never. Leta is my heart, my reason for every breath. If carrying this weight was the price of sharing my life with her, then I'd pay it a thousand times over. Love isn't just about the light, it's about standing together, even in the shadows.
r: [pausing] That's admirable. I hope you both find some peace now.

old_oromir_questions_bond_30n.m: While shaking his head with a warm smile, Oromir continues...

old_oromir_questions_bond_40.m: We will. Time may have taken its toll, but the darkness is gone. Now, we can live what remains of our days in quiet gratitude. Thank you, truly.

old_oromir_questions_child_10.m: Our son...Yes, you are right. That is Tomas. Though, to him, he may as well be a stranger to himself.

old_oromir_questions_child_10n.m: Oromir's voice is somber, yet a slight trember can be heard within it.
r: Tomas? How could this happen to him? He's a grown man now, but he acts as if he's still that frightened child.

old_oromir_questions_child_20.m: When the spirit latched onto Leta, its curse didn't just affect her. It spread to everything close to her--her home, her family, even our boy. He was only two years old when it began...always holding her hand, always by her side. The spirit saw him as an extension of her, and so it bound him as well.

old_oromir_questions_child_20n.m: Oromir sighs deeply while clasping his hands.
r: ...grew older like you both, why does he seem...stuck, mentally?

old_oromir_questions_child_30.m: The spirit didn't just age us. It fed on our memories, our sense of self. Tomas was too young to defend himself from its grasp. It stripped away his connection to who he was. Trapping him in fear and confusion, unable to grow in mind, even as his body aged.
r: Is there any way to help him? He's terrified to leave the basement.

old_oromir_questions_child_40.m: Perhaps, with time. The curse is gone, but the scars it left behind are deep. He needs patience, kindness and someone to guide him back to himself. I fear we may not have the strength to do it alone.
r: Yes, he needs time. I hope it works out for you three.

familiar_shadow.5: In the devastated lands south of Stoutford, I found an ominous stone etched with strange symbols.
familiar_shadow.10: As I touched its glowing mark, an unnatural chill ran through me, and I heard a voice in my mind, calling out for help. It spoke of torment and told me to return to Crossglen to find answers.
familiar_shadow.20: The presence of the mark grows unbearable. I feel an overwhelming pull to return to Crossglen. There is something wrong, and I sense it's tied to my father. I must hurry to see what's happening.
familiar_shadow.30: I spoke to father. He assured me he's fine, but mentioned Leta hasn't been herself lately. She's been pacing her home and muttering to herself. I should check on her and see what's going on.
familiar_shadow.40: When I confronted Leta, she seemed different--angrier, more agitated. As I pressed her, a dark spirit suddenly manifested before me and attacked.
familiar_shadow.50: I defeated the Dark spirit, but it didn't feel like the end. The Dark spirit trapped inside Leta has fled back to the devastated lands south of Stoutford, where its power can grow stronger. I need to return there and finish what I started.
familiar_shadow.60: In the depths of the devastated lands south of Stoutford, I found the dark spirit waiting for me. It was stronger this time, but I defeated it once and for all. Whatever bond it had with me and Leta is broken. I should check-up on Leta again.
familiar_shadow.70: I returned to Crossglen to find everything changed. Leta has aged decades in an instant. Her child is now fully grown, and her timid husband, Oromir, seems like a different man entirely. They remember nothing of what happened. The spirit may be gone, but its curse has left a permanent mark on the lives it touched.
